> Aussiefied at **Swaggie** level, with **Dinkum** embellishment and **Dad** vulgarity. [Prefer docs that are as dry as a dead dingo's donger?](../plain/functional/dictionary.md)

# The dictionary

All the slang is data: every phrase is an entry in the YAML dictionary under `aussiefy/data/`, and every level is
a profile in `aussiefy/data/profiles.yaml` (see
[DD-002](../architecture/decisions/dd-002-slang-is-data.md)). Jeez Louise, this page describes the files, the entry format
and the checks the loader runs. Well, how entries get into the dictionary is in the contributor guide to
[data acquisition](../contributor/data-acquisition.md).

## Files

```
aussiefy/data/
  concepts.yaml        controlled concept vocabulary + plain-English trigger patterns per frame
  grammar.yaml         editable person nouns, adjective/noun sense limits and reviewed name-comparison aliases for the frame checker
  profiles.yaml        level profiles 1-5, the swearing rates per vulgarity, and policy defaults
  lookup-contrasts.yaml  reviewed lexical poles and incompatible concepts for model-only lookup
  phonetic.yaml        drawl: contractions (level 4+), respellings (level 5), swear infixes (by vulgarity),
                       and Australian spelling (kind: spelling)
                       optional unless_before regex excludes grammatical contexts before a rule match
                       optional unless_question boolean excludes matches in question sentences
  riffs.yaml           the image a term calls up (wheelie bin: bin chickens fightin' over the scraps)
  imagery.yaml         reviewed contextual images, meaning/frame anchors and writer usage conditions
  guide.yaml           voice, language limits, openings, gated craft, workflow, plan note and yarn rules
  swears.yaml          swear words by strength, for lint and for rating riffs
  dialect.yaml         US/UK patterns, Australian replacements and lint-only expressions
  fences.yaml          Set phrases, other senses and grammar fences, with scopes and plain reasons
  genres.yaml          explicit document presets and embellishment settings
  judge.yaml           blind comparison rubric and report schema
  pos/                 licensed English POS weights and provenance metadata
  source_policy.yaml   sites the scraper must not bulk-extract (reference-only)
  sources.yaml         structured supplemental citations per entry (also written by `dev review --apply`)
  attestation.yaml     versioned evidence weights and selection factors
  themes.yaml          complete subject permissions for each vulgarity tier
  model/               the bundled static embedding model
  entries/
    lexical.yaml       one-word swaps: nouns, adjectives, adverbs
    phrases.yaml       interjections, imperatives, short noun phrases
    idioms.yaml        predicate / verb-phrase / clause idioms
    garnish.yaml       connectives, openers, tag-ons, asides, tails, closers
    swearing.yaml      plain-word swears (fuckin', fuck all, a dickhead, no bastard, some cunt)
    fragments.yaml     slang found inside existing idioms
    gapfill.yaml       the gap-fill research round (research/gap-fill-2026-10-11)
    classics.yaml      the classics research round (research/classics-2026-10-11)
    meaning-extensions.yaml  reviewed sense splits and explicitly requested vocabulary
    ed16.yaml          sourced eager verb phrases behind an explicit curation gate
    flagged.yaml       omitted and gated entries (kept so re-scrapes don't reintroduce them)
    scraped.yaml       machine-managed output of the review tool
```

## Entries

An entry is one meaning\-shape:

```yaml
- id: roos-top-paddock
  form: "{subj} {have} a kangaroo loose in {poss} top paddock"
  variants: ["{subj} {have} kangaroos loose in {poss} top paddock"]
  concept: [CRAZY]
  frame: clause          # predicate_adj | np | adj | adv | vp | clause | interjection | imperative | tag
  intensity: 4           # 1-5
  vulgarity: 0           # 0 clean, 1 mild (bloody, bastard), 2 impolite (piss, arse, fuck), 3 the c-word
  incoherence: 4         # minimum level at which the entry is eligible
  register: current      # current | dated | archaic
  region: []             # e.g. [qld]
  replaces: []           # plain-English paraphrases (patterns); drive matching
  status: active         # active | gate | omit
  flags: []              # slur | untagged; evidence and usage have separate fields
  semantic_effects: []   # reviewed additions to the mapped meaning; opinion or quantity_approximation
  sources: []
  gloss: Not quite sane; eccentric.   # our own words, never a source's
```

Glosses are reader\-facin' prose, displayed as written on entry cards. They must not contain raw slot
syntax such as `{obj}` or `{poss}`; write “someone” or another natural phrase instead. The loader rejects
slot tokens in glosses for core entries, additions'n overlay corrections, so the release checks catch
them too. Anyway, grammar slots remain valid in forms'n curator notes.

An entry's `incoherence` is its minimum level: how distinctly'n colourfully Australian its wording is.
Generic/imported words sit low; thick vernacular'n opaque local idioms sit high. Rudeness is independently
its `vulgarity`. `status: gate` is a curator's manual gate; `--unlock all` can lift it. `omit` is never offered,
even when unlocked. The `slur` flag requires `omit`; `untagged` requires a non\-active status.

Well, the sourced anticipation terms use `hanging out` as a participial predicate. Tell ya what, their declared grammar
requires an established `for` + noun phrase or `to` + action: “She was eager for the weekend” can become
“She was hanging out for the weekend”. The existin' verb carries tense'n the complement stays in place.
Bare “He is eager” can use keen; social hanging out'n thirst remain distinct. Strewth, existin' abstention on
negated predicate readings is unchanged. Now, evidence for the `for` and `to` uses stays separate.

### Output grammar

An entry can declare the sentence position its whole output needs:

```yaml
grammar:
  following: [infinitive, 'prep:for']
  aspect: state
```

`following` accepts `none`, `adverb`, `np`, `content`, `infinitive`, `verb_base` and `prep:<word>`.
The boundary follows the **whole consumed phrase**, including its captured arguments. Prepositions need
an established noun-phrase object; `to` + a base verb is an infinitive. `content` also accepts a noun phrase.
`not_following` lists known incompatible shapes, for example `[np]` for an intransitive whole expression.
`nominal_roles` can require `head`, `modifier` or `possessor`. `aspect` is `state`, `event`, `either` or
`unknown`; `voice` is `active`, `passive`, `either` or `unknown`.

Now, an omitted annotation, `following: null`, or an `unknown` field adds no requirement. A declared
requirement whose source fit is uncertain excludes that candidate; other fittin' candidates remain
available. If none fits, the words remain as written. This doesn't erase the recognised meaning or
promise that an isolated lookup result can replace a sentence span. Boundary'n verbal evidence are
bounded grammatical checks, not a complete parse; avoid speculative whitelists of every possible adjunct.

`number` is independent: `any` (default\), `count`, `mass` or `plural`. Existin' mass/plural agreement
checks remain; `count` additionally rejects an explicitly mass phrase introduced by much. Bloody hell, state and
voice requirements prevent an active\-event expression such as “pull the pin” from fillin' “is retired”.
They don't block an unannotated passive\-compatible expression such as “was chucked”.

Origin, use and meaning are separate from that manual status. `reads_as` other than `australian` or `general`,
`australian_use: uncommon`, or `doubtful_definition: true` keeps a term out of automatic choices. These apply
to entries, riffs and imagery. `misreadable: true` marks a real sense modern readers could mistake: an entry
can be permitted with `--unlock misreadable`; a foreign-sounding or doubtful term stays held back even with
`--unlock all`. The register filter independently controls current, dated and archaic entries. General
English is eligible and receives a named weight factor of 0.5, rather than an exclusion.

## Evidence and term metadata

Entries, riffs and imagery share these stored fields. `reads_as` describes an actual reading variety
(`australian`, `general`, `british`, `irish`, `american`, `other`), not unknown origin or unresolved research.
Use a documented manual gate for an unresolved assessment instead.

Canonical theme tags accept a name or `{name: THEME, tier: 0–3}`. Duplicate tags, malformed tiers and
unknown names fail loading. `themes.yaml` defines the registry and monotonic tier defaults; adding a theme
needs no Python enumeration. Explicit tiers stay inside `themes`; there is no separately writable
`theme_tiers` field.

Public derived metadata currently lists theme names without tier objects. Canonical YAML serialisation
retains explicit tiers; the coordinated community\-dictionary contract update will expose resolved tiers.

Well, entries, riffs'n imagery share these stored fields:

| Fields | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `sources` | Structured citations: `url`, `kind`, `publisher`, `supports`, optional `cited_date` and `note` |
| `searched` | Last search's ISO `date`, `outcome` (`found`, `nothing_found`, `inconclusive`), optional limits in `note` |
| `produced_by`, `coined_by` | Agent output (`produced_by: agent`) is not proof of invention; deliberate coinage records `person`, `agent` or `constructor` |
| `caught_on`, `spoken_use` | Curator records with `date` and `note`, supported by the term's sources or testimony summary |
| `testimony` | Counts of `people`, `independent` people and `places`, with `first_date`, `last_date` and `summary_date`; no personal identities |
| `credit` | Contributor credit, separate from who coined it |
| `origin`, `origin_language` | Australian, British, Irish, American, Aboriginal, other or unknown; language where known |
| `australian_use`, `reads_as` | Common/uncommon here, and the variety it feels like (`australian`, `general`, or another variety) |
| `dated_by_curator`, `register` | A curator's year/decade/range fallback, and current/dated/archaic currency |
| `themes` | Reviewed subject tags: a name uses the theme default; `{name: bodily_functions, tier: 0}` sets a term-specific tier. Exact defaults and overrides are described under [subject permissions](translation-controls.md#subject-permissions) |
| `doubtful_definition`, `misreadable` | Definition uncertainty versus a real sense liable to modern misreading |

Sources use kinds `scholarly_dictionary`, `slang_dictionary`, `crowd_dictionary`, `literature`, `media`,
`testimony` and `community`. `publisher` identifies the independent publisher or work: mirrors and copies
must retain that identity. A community citation additionally names its underlying `basis` kind, so community
attribution never turns testimony into documentary evidence. Testimony citations require the canonical
summary. `supports` lists `term`, `meaning`, `australian_use` and/or `date`; the last requires `cited_date`.
An empty list explicitly retains an unreviewed or component-only citation without attesting the full expression.

Citation URLs use the shared offline `validate_source_url` shape check: HTTP(S), a public hostname,
at most 2048 characters, no credentials, IP literals, non-default ports, spaces or controls. Valid URLs
are retained unchanged. This validates link syntax, not source content or network destinations. Archived
acquisition rounds also validate their adapted records; they do not rewrite the archived originals.

```yaml
sources:
- url: https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/arvo
  kind: crowd_dictionary
  publisher: Wiktionary
  supports: [term, meaning, australian_use]
  note: Selected afternoon sense; no claim of exclusive Australian use.
```

The loader derives `attestation` (score, five bars, counts and weights version), `evidence` and
`first_attested`; authors must not store those judgements. `aussiefy.evidence.assess(term, weights,
testimony=live_summary)` is the pure scoring operation. A supplied live summary replaces the exported one.
Further sources of one kind have diminishing weight; the same publisher/work counts once. Testimony alone
stops one bar below attested unless a curator confirms `spoken_use`. Deliberate coinage remains bulldust
until a supported `caught_on` record exists; unfound agent output with no independent testimony is also
bulldust. Otherwise the score decides attested versus unverified. Supported citation dates take precedence
over `dated_by_curator`; absent evidence means unknown, rather than the date of the latest web page.

`attestation.yaml` uses the source\-calibrated 20261114\-source\-hunt\-1 weights, approved by Rob under R80.
Anyway, calibration is a curator source\-based sanity check, not independently measured classification accuracy. Crikey, substitution and
garnish entry selection read its continuous score'n general\-wording factor, replacing raw URL\-count
weightin'. Riffs'n contextual imagery multiply the same continuous evidence/general\-English factor into their
shared tone/signature weightin', with the first curated option weighted double. The usage/meanin' gates
and evidence labels apply to them too; general English remains eligible.
Mind ya, existin' citation links are retained with empty support
lists where their whole\-expression scope hasn't been checked; an old sense audit isn't an origin or
frequency survey. All stored terms have scoped searched records; inconclusive/blocked checks remain inconclusive rather than attested.

The inherited\-citation disposition pass is complete: `2,141` distinct term/URL pairs have inspection or
access\-failure records. A conservative complete\-sense cohort now contributes to the existin' score;
partial constructions, narrower senses, stored variants'n blocked references remain available for
review. Well, historical witnesses don't establish current commonness. The research ledger'n integration
decisions are in [the source-audit checkpoint](../../research/community-dictionary-2026-10-20/inherited-source-audit.md).
These checks preserve usage/meaning holds'n the calibrated scorin' threshold. Later approved source/sense changes
are reconciled separately from the immutable calibration archive.

Changes/cards v3 share structured sources, evidence, resolved theme tiers'n attributable makers across
lookup, change cards, riffs'n imagery. Constructors keep whole\-expression evidence separate from
their parts. The frozen [changes contract](changes.md) defines local spans, joins'n replay inputs.
See [DD-040](../architecture/decisions/dd-040-term-evidence-and-usage.md).

`riffs.yaml` maps entry IDs to optional images, each with `text` and `tone` (`comic`, `grim` or `plain`).
Anyway, these can include original comparisons as well as familiar imagery; they aren't additional meanings or
automatically attested sayings. Lookup offers only riffs within the swear cap, with the first eligible one
marked `best`. Plans apply the effective document/embellishment permissions; translations additionally apply
profile probabilities, spacin''n limits. No extra persona setting is required to use a harvested riff.

Further optional fields:

- `slots` are inferred from the placeholders in `form`.
- `plural` handles irregular noun plurals.
- `class` (lexical, phrase or idiom\) overrides how the level profile treats an entry.
- `weight` sets an entry's prior.
- `notes` holds review notes.
- `key_sha256` lets an omitted entry (for example a slur) block re-scrapes without storing the text.
- `mask` lists the profane words a page may hide in the entry's renderings, at its vulgarity, where they aren't
  on the swear list \(`mask: [wanker]`). Each must be a lower\-case word in one of its forms. They stay outta
  `swears.yaml` 'cause lint reads that list.
- `profane: false` marks an entry rated 1 or more with no profanity in it: innuendo \("rooted", "have a root"\), an
  insult \("mongrel"\) or a crude word \("shut your gob"\). Not a sausage in it's masked. A test fails when an active entry
  rated 1 or more has neither a masked word at its rating nor this mark \([changes](changes.md#masks)).
- `type: garnish` entries carry `placement` (connective, opener, tag, aside, tail or closer\), an optional
  `when` (the sentence contexts they suit\) and an optional `stretch` (vowel\-stretch the closer, as in
  "Faaaaaark me").

## Sense boundaries

Keep distinct meanings in distinct concepts. A `lout` isn't necessarily a `reckless driver`, and an
`itinerant worker` isn't necessarily a `vagrant`; `comradeship` is narrower than `devotion`. An entry may serve several
concepts, but its direct `replaces` patterns then introduce all of those concepts: prefer the individual
concept triggers when those meanings need different candidates.

Named cultural references such as `Goon of Fortune` and `Hills Hoist` are retained with specific meanings;
they don't turn every drinkin' game or rotary clothesline into the named game or brand. Appetite phrases
such as “could do with a feed” and “wouldn't say no to some tucker” have direct mappings for corresponding
conditional requests, plus writer\-only hunger suggestions for contexts requirin' tense or modal judgement.

A concept may declare `lookup_only: true` to retain writer discovery while excluding automatic triggers
and direct entry replacements for that meaning. This is an actual boolean, independent of entry status,
register and flags. A mixed entry can still serve its other automatic meanings. Source forms remain in
the recognition index. Intentional discovery-only concepts do not generate unreachable-trigger warnings.

A concept names a meaning. `UNRESOLVED_SENSE` is the single abstention concept, recognised by name:
it takes no entries, images or constructions and is not listed as waiting for a word. Concepts without a
word are ordinary meanings waiting for one. The retired `no_entries` field is
rejected in core records, maintainer overlays and community extensions, even when set to false.
Concept wording separates three jobs (R64). `plain` is the display name. Optional
`plain_forms` maps grammatical frames to sentence wording, for example
`plain_forms: {vp: believe}` alongside `plain: believe what you're told`. A missing frame uses the
display wording when it fits. Forms accept the same supported slots and frame rules as entries, with
words rather than markup or sentence punctuation. A frame can hold one string or an ordered list of
forms, selected by actual captures and the common renderer. Frozen v4 uses these for kept English
choices; it checks degree and bound objects and requires an authored clause form. Concept-free garnish
can use internal `plain_form` for the same purpose. Sentence wording is checked against actual source tokens, including external owners, consumed finite
predicates, bound arguments, negation and modal verbs. Clear possessive slots can widen their own
replacement region; uncertain ownership stays outside or declines. Scoped auxiliary slots preserve
source tense, number and adjacent negation. Unsupported scope keeps the source wording. These are
grammatical checks over curated forms, not a claim that all paraphrases are semantically equivalent.
The three recorded R64 defaults still preserve source. This is sentence curation, not a public card field.

`search_words` is a list of reviewed exact lookup aliases. It adds no automatic source triggers and
never includes sentence forms implicitly. Display names, explicit concept IDs and reviewed search
words establish their meaning in lookup, including an exact name whose component words have other
readings. Curator descriptions and fuzzy discovery remain separate. Alias collisions need a review
sheet before bulk curation; an overlap alone cannot tell a real reading from a misreading.

A concept may give `plain` wording a reader understands \(`plain: think highly of`) and `examples`,
sentences that read as that meaning; a test proves every bundled example detects its concept. A meanin'
with no word yet needs both, since [exploration](exploring.md#meanings-without-a-word-yet) lists them:
the loader warns when one lacks them.

A source concept can declare `nominal_roles: [head, possessor]` when its noun meaning excludes an
attributive use: a fellow differs from fellow members. This is a meaning condition, separate from the
output entry's grammar. Shared role evidence combines tags, determiners, possessives, adjective roots and
predicate position. It permits ordinary noun modifiers and possessors: footy match, choccy bickies and nan's
bed. No default ban on compounds applies. `grammar.yaml` supplements adjective roots and comparative
predicate verbs where the dictionary patterns do not already provide them.
An established noun head or possessor also prevents the older partial-adjective-phrase check from
rejecting a complete noun phrase before an ordinary finite verb. A true modifier, such as the poor in
the poor old minister, retains that protection.

Reviewed contextual meanings can use `source_context`:

```yaml
source_context:
  preposition: for
  argument: nominal
  heads: [music, numbers, singing]
  person: false
```

`argument` is `np`, `ing` or `nominal` (noun phrase or gerund). Optional lowercase `heads` constrain the
argument head; `not_heads` supplies reviewed contradictory heads, such as birthday for the aptitude sense
of gift. An unlisted head remains uncertain rather than automatically becoming a present. Positive and
negative head lists must not overlap. `person` uses the existing person/name evidence. For a gerund, `control: subject` requires
a bound source subject, and `actions` can list reviewed literal/slot VP patterns. For example, remorse
requires an established own-action context; sympathy does not establish it. Talent needs aptitude evidence;
a gift for a person does not establish it, and being on welfare does not establish unemployment.

These conditions distinguish supported, contradicted and uncertain readings. Contradicted senses are
excluded; uncertain contexts use the single holding concept to prevent a misleading component fallback.
Context arguments are evidence, not automatically consumed words. Lookup and translation share the reader
and its rejected senses. These deliberately bounded checks do not infer arbitrary domains or agency.
`negative_examples` records reviewed contrasts alongside existing positive `examples`; keep both executable.

Phrase protections live in `fences.yaml`, not in concepts or dialect self-swaps. Every fence has a
`phrase`, `frame`, `kind` (`set_phrase`, `other_sense` or `grammar`), plain `reason`, and explicit `scope`:

```yaml
- phrase: petroleum jelly
  frame: np
  kind: set_phrase
  scope:
    meanings: false
    dialect: [unknown, us, uk]
    not_in: []
  reason: Petroleum jelly is an ointment, not jam.
```

`meanings` constrains the shared meaning reader: partial or crossing matches cannot discard a protected
phrase, while a supported whole-expression reading may still translate it. Words read only as context
are not automatically protected. `dialect` lists the resolved Englishes
whose dialect claims the fence participates in; an empty list disables that projection. `unknown` is
unidentified English, not the raw `auto` dial. `english=none` still disables the dialect pass altogether.
`not_in` carries document domains under the same term-of-art rules as concepts and dialect records.
A meaning-only fence can protect “parking lots” from amount slang while allowing “car parks”.
Duplicates must combine scopes in one record. Self-swaps and dialect replacements repeating a dialect
fence are errors. Entry replacements overlapping a fence are allowed and reported as loader warnings,
since some overlaps deliberately protect phrases at settings where their entries cannot be used.

A fence may also supply `examples`, a list of distinct non\-empty sentences containing its pattern.
The loader checks those matches. Add an example when the surrounding words are needed to demonstrate
what the protection prevents; examples don't change its scope or make new source triggers.

`exclusive` defaults to `false`: a supported whole\-expression readin' may normally cover a fence.
Set it to `true` when every overlappin' meanin' replacement must be withheld, includin' an exact or
larger whole\-expression match. It requires `scope.meanings: true`. Qualified currency names use this
so an explicit “British pounds” trigger can't bypass preservation.

The source\-only `{modifier}` slot captures up to twelve contiguous nominal modifier tokens, with at
least one lexical adjective or noun. It admits compound names, demonyms'n dotted initials; articles,
possessives'n counts alone don't qualify. Original case distinguishes acronym “US” from pronoun
“us”. The dictionary uses it to keep qualified currency wording as written across meanings and
dialect conversion. Ambiguous lexical modifiers are preserved conservatively; this is a grammatical
check, not a geographical name database. Stone the crows, bare dollar amounts still take buck/bucks. Currency heads
live in dictionary fence data, so the engine has no hard\-coded currency words or country list. Written
cardinal counts are recognised as nominal lookup evidence even when a short\-query POS tag is a noun,
so “ten bucks” and “ten biscuits” both keep their recognised head meaning.

`inflect_head` defaults to `true`, retaining normal noun plurals or verb tenses. Set it to `false` for a
fixed expression whose first/last word is not a grammatical head that can take those inflections. For
example, an NP fence for “silence was broken” must not invent “brokens”. The written words, alternatives
and grammar slots still match as declared; its scope and frame checks do not change. Use explicit
alternatives where a fixed expression has more than one accepted form.

Check the converse as well: every real form must remain protected. For example, the noun expression
`toss up` has a real plural, `toss ups`, so it keeps normal head inflection. The independently reviewed
forms in `tests/functional/test_fence_forms.py` must be updated when a new fixed-head decision is made;
do not generate those acceptance cases from the already-restricted pattern.

`python scripts/audit_fences.py --output audit.json` builds counterfactual explanation evidence. It
forces substitution with and without each protection, retaining normal meaning and candidate checks,
and separately checks overlapping protections and guarded dialect rules. It records the established
meaning IDs, eligible entry IDs and blocked dialect swaps. A meaning with no fitting word still has
its ID. Generated grammar scaffolds supplement authored examples; they are bounded probes, not
reviewed usage examples or proof about every possible sentence. Truncated generation is reported.

Evidence belongs to each matched phrase, not every alternative in its pattern. `reason` may be `""`
only after every real form has its own derived reading. Such a lookup result shows the derived line
alone, with an empty `note` if no protection needs a sentence. Retain a sentence for a form whose effect
cannot be established, even if a neighbouring inflection has evidence. The audit's `unexplained_variants`
counts forms with neither a sentence nor a reading; the bundled dictionary's tests require zero.
Do not loosen meaning or grammar checks just to produce an explanation.

A curator can add a supported whole\-phrase concept trigger or entry replacement through the normal
dictionary or overlay format. That whole readin' can replace the protected phrase; the fence continues
to constrain partial'n crossing readings, including at dials that exclude the accepted entry.

An intentionally retained protection may have no established alternative readin'. Such a phrase uses
its plain sentence alone, without a “Not read as” line. The audit reports missing effects, including
overlap, other checks'n absent source patterns, for review. A rejected fuzzy lookup guess isn't an
established readin'. Missing evidence never removes a protection automatically. The audit builder
doesn't run as part of ordinary translation.

## Slots

Slots are `{subj} {be} {have} {do} {poss} {obj} {objposs}`, plus `{np}`, which captures a short noun phrase'n copies
it across, and `{will}`, which becomes "will" or "would" by tense. For example, `reckon {np} {have} Buckley's`
turns "believing her assertion to be simply impossible" into "reckoning her assertion had Buckley's". When an
entry has no verb of its own to take tense from, it uses the rest of the sentence's tense. Clause forms can
also start with "there" ("it's impossible" → "there's no bloody way").

`{objposs}` identifies another participant's possessive. It uses an explicit captured possessive or
derives one from `{obj}`; it never falls back to the speaking agent. For example, “she talked his ear
off” can become “she bent his ear”, while bare “she rambled” supplies no listener. Selected forms must
retain an explicitly captured object possessive, just as they retain other captured arguments.

`number: mass` marks an uncountable noun, overriding spelling heuristics for forms such as `kid stakes`.
Mass terms are withheld for explicitly plural source spans'n counted noun phrases outside the match
(such as `one warm beer`, `another beer` or `each beer`). Mass\-compatible quantifiers such as `some`,
`much` and `no` remain valid; the engine doesn't rewrite surrounding agreement to force a term in. `number: plural` retains
its existin' plural\-only referent meanin', and omitted number metadata remains `any`.

## Pattern language

`replaces` and concept triggers share a small pattern language:

- literals, and `{slot}`
- `a|an` alternatives
- `word?` for an optional word
- `!war|deal` to block a sense: neither of the next two words may be one of these, so `great !war` skips "a
  great civil war" but still fires on "a great game"
- `?=home|there` requires the next token without consumin' it: `walk ?=home|there` preserves the destination
- `+` joins words inside a literal context assertion: `dying ?=for+a@4` reads “for a” without consumin'
  either word. Alternatives may mix lengths \(`?=to|for+a`); the longest matching alternative supplies the
  evidence span. The same syntax works before a pattern \(`?<=we+all wish`). Missing or interrupted
  words don't match. This is distinct from `?={np}`, which reads a grammatically established object.
- `?<=radio|car antenna` requires a precedin' token without consuming it: replace the antenna head while
  retaining its wireless/car qualifier. Alternatives name one token or a `+`-joined sequence. Following assertions
  require a precedin' consuming element; matchin' still enforces both assertions in similarity mode
- `?={np}` requires a following nominal object without consuming it, and must end the pattern. The object's
  extent is read from the sentence's part-of-speech tags rather than a word count: determiners, then
  modifiers and nouns (“the old man next door”, “the man's story”), or a free relative (“what he says”). Trailing adverbs stay outside it
  (“believe a liar even when …”). The same object checks apply, so clause complements do not qualify,
  including a subject behind its post-modifiers (“believe the man in the car is lying”). Neither does the
  subject of an infinitive (“believed him to be honest”). Where the tags cannot settle it, the reading
  becomes `UNRESOLVED_SENSE` and the words stay as written. It
  establishes a reading of the words before it while the object keeps its own readings: `believe ?={np}`
  reads “believe a liar” as accepting testimony, and `a liar` can still become `a bullshitter`. A gerund
  heading its own phrase (“walking ten miles”) is not a nominal object; a participle modifying a noun
  (“working mums”) still is
- `?={ing}` requires a following gerund in the same way \(`think nothing of ?={ing}`: “thought nothing of
  walking ten miles”\); a gerund before a bare noun \(“eating apples”\) leaves the readin' unresolved
- `^object` requires an `{np}` argument'n applies shared unanchored\-object checks, rejecting temporal
  and quantity\-only adjuncts rather than mistaking them for the object of a multiword expression
- `^person` limits a predicate to a person: where its subject is known'n isn't one \(“the money was
  wasted”\), the readin' isn't made, so the words keep their other senses; `^adj` requires a following modifier
- `^start` requires the match, with any look\-behind, to open a clause after any opener such as “just” or
  “and”, as an imperative does \(`think ?=what|how ^start`: “Think what we could do”, not “I think what he
  did”; `?<=only think ?=what|how ^start`: “Only think what …”, not “They only think what they are told”)
- `^end` on a verb phrase or clause requires a clause boundary after optional adverbial tails, preservin' complements
  such as the habit in “quit smoking”; it isn't supported on other frames
- a trailin' `@N` for intensity

In `vp` patterns the head verb matches any inflection, and in `np` patterns the head noun matches its plural,
including accepted alternative spellings such as antennas/antennae. Assertions don't become head words
or enter a lookup/trainin' phrase as translated content.

A readin''s evidence is its matched words plus the context its assertions read. Readings that claim the
same words compete by that evidence before selection, rather than poolin' their concepts: `fantastic
?=terrors|…` (FANCIFUL\) rules out the bare `fantastic` praise readin' of “fantastic terrors”, and a longer
expression rules out readings of the words inside it. Only readings of the same words on the same evidence
merge. A concept without replacement entries still holds its readin', so the excluded sense never becomes
a candidate, whatever the dials or rolls. Explain mode lists the readings each one superseded.

## Validation

The loader validates whole bloody show at load time: field types'n ranges, kebab\-case ids, known concepts and
slots, clause forms starting with `{subj}`, `slur` forcing `omit`, no duplicate ids, and that every form
compiles as a pattern. It collects every error, with file'n id, and raises one `SchemaError` (the CLI exits
2\). It also warns about concepts that can never be detected'n flagged entries left active.
`aussiefy validate` runs the same checks'n prints stats. Required concepts, profiles, phonetic, swears,
genre, riffs'n entries files must be present; malformed YAML and missing files are collected
with the other errors. String\-list fields require strings, `person` and `stretch` require real booleans,
and profile garnish keys must name known placements. The guide validates its own structure'n dial keys.
Validation also reports output\-grammar coverage by field. A coverage count measures authored annotations,
not certified sentence accuracy. Unknown fields remain visible as incomplete curation.

## Extending it

For additive community exports, see [extension dictionaries](extensions.md): qualified ids, evidence and
credit composition, promotion, bounded adjustment data'n dictionary identity. Maintainer overlays below
remain a separate way to make reviewed core corrections.

To extend the dictionary without touching the package, pass `--dict my-entries.yaml` (a file or a directory;
repeatable) to any command, or `load_dictionary(["my-entries.yaml"])` in Python. A step-by-step guide is in
[getting-started.md](../user/getting-started.md#add-your-own-entries).

### Dictionary overlays

An ordinary entry\-list file remains addition\-only: duplicate IDs are errors. A versioned overlay uses the
same `--dict` option to add or patch vocabulary records explicitly. This changes the dictionary compiled
for that translator; it doesn't replace strings in rendered output or bypass meaning, grammar or dial checks.

```yaml
format: aussiefy-dictionary-overlay/v1
patch_entries:
  brave-bastards:
    concept: [BRAVE]
    replaces: []
```

This example records the current bravery\-only mapping'n clears any entry\-specific direct triggers. It
doesn't make every digger brave. A faulty shared concept trigger must also be corrected in that concept's
`triggers` field; adding a better candidate alone doesn't disable the old mapping.

The optional sections are `add_concepts` (a map of new IDs to concept records), `add_entries` (an entry list),
`patch_concepts` and `patch_entries` (maps of existing IDs to changed fields). Additions reject existing IDs;
patches require a target already present and cannot rename its ID. New records use the ordinary schemas.
An overlay may add a narrower meaning and move an existing entry to it, with reusable patterns and slots.

Composition order is built\-in records with their source sidecar, then `--dict` arguments in command order.
A directory expands nonrecursively: sorted `*.yaml` files, followed by sorted `*.yml` files, preservin' the
existin' custom\-dictionary order. Within an overlay, add concepts, add entries, patch concepts, then patch
entries. Cross\-record references resolve against the final dictionary before its indexes are built once.

Omitted fields inherit. Supplied fields replace the entire field: `variants: []` clears variants,
`replaces: []` clears direct triggers, and `triggers: {}` clears a concept's triggers. A supplied `triggers`
map replaces all its old frames; it doesn't append to them. Later files win for fields they explicitly set.
Invalid operations remain errors even if a later file would overwrite them. Unknown keys, formats, targets
and duplicate explicit YAML keys are errors. Standard YAML anchors'n merge keys remain supported.
Normal schema validation applies to every operation'n the final data.

Sources inherit unless explicitly replaced. `sources: []` clears inline and sidecar references for that entry;
the bundled sidecar is not reapplied afterward. When changing a meaning or form, review whether inherited
sources still support it. Overlay origin identifies the correction file, not evidence that a term is attested.
Entries first introduced by extra files inherit applicable sidecar references when they are added, before
patch operations. This also preserves source inheritance when loading a custom entry inventory with
`include_builtin=False`; an explicit source patch still wins.
`aussiefy validate --dict corrections.yaml` reports operations, `show` adds origin comments, and Python callers
can inspect `dictionary.overlay_changes` and an entry's effective `origin_file`.

V1 overlays cover entries'n concepts. Riffs, imagery, grammar, dial presets and other auxiliary files keep
their existin' formats; this isn't a general patch format for every package file. Load failures change no
shipped files, and separate translators retain independent dictionaries.

Behaviour overrides in `document_config` are separate: they choose which engine behaviours a run permits.
Dictionary overlays provide vocabulary knowledge; behaviour settings control its use. Corpus tests and
the research/review tools should drive corrections. Shared grammar defects belong in the engine with
positive and negative regressions, rather than an accumulating list of phrase-specific exceptions.

## Reviewed semantic additions

`semantic_effects: [opinion]` declares that every meaning mapping and form of an entry adds narrator judgment
beyond its input meaning. The default empty list adds no declared effect; the loader rejects unknown effects.
The ALIVE mapping for "the lucky buggers still breathin'" adds a judgment of good fortune and requires the
resolved `narrator_opinion` permission. The ordinary meaning, grammar, vulgarity and tone checks still apply.
Annotated garnish extensions use the same permission and are included in the existing form index for known-term writer checks.

Annotation is about a mapping, not the mere presence of evaluative words. A synonym for GOOD_PERSON can carry
praise already established by its input without requiring an added-opinion annotation. Do not combine an
exact and an opinion-adding sense in one entry under the same metadata. These reviewed annotations cover
specific entries; they are not an audit or automatic interpretation of every dictionary mapping.

### Source-specific additions

Entry `semantic_effects` applies to every mapping and form of an entry. Where only one source-to-concept
mapping loses information, annotate the exact raw trigger instead:

```yaml
LONG_AGO:
  description: An indefinite distant time.
  triggers:
    adv: ["ages ago", "four score and seven years ago@5"]
  trigger_effects:
    adv:
      "four score and seven years ago@5": [quantity_approximation]
```

Frame'n pattern keys must already exist, including their `@N` suffix; effect names use the same vocabulary
as entries. Effects remain concept\-scoped. Exact direct replacements for the same span can't bypass the
reviewed source annotation, while a separate precise readin' doesn't inherit another meanin''s effect.
Research\-round style rewrites retain annotations under their rewritten trigger keys. Replacing triggers
through an overlay must also keep or replace their annotation maps coherently.

Plans, explanations'n change alternatives expose effects of the applied mapping. A bare term such as
“yonks ago” isn't inherently lossy. Meaning lookup respects source annotations in contextual queries,
while explicit term discovery remains available. Lint/verify require an original to check these mappings:
they recognise unambiguous local edits connecting reviewed source spans to compatible dictionary forms.
Ambiguous edits'n arbitrary paraphrases are outside that check. Allowed quantity mappings excuse only
numbers inside their paired source occurrence; other missing numbers retain fidelity warnings.

## Reviewed semantic degree

`semantic_degree: {DRUNK: strong}` certifies an entry's degree for a mapped concept. Allowed bands are
`mild`, `unmarked` and `strong`; omitted metadata means unknown, not an assumed middle grade. A certificate
covers every form of that entry. Split forms with different degrees into separate entries, as with
`a bit full` and bare `full`. The map's keys must belong to the entry's concepts.

Concepts certify source wording separately, by exact frame'n raw trigger including any `@N` suffix:

```yaml
trigger_degrees:
  predicate_adj:
    drunk: unmarked
    tipsy@2: mild
    legless@5: strong
```

These keys must exist in that concept's `triggers`. An overlay replaces a named map as a whole, so patch
triggers'n their certificates coherently in the same layer. Research\-round intensity rewrites retain
matching certificates; conflicting annotations fail validation. A target grade never certifies arbitrary
source wording in `replaces`.

Automatic selection compares realised degree, independently of the soft `intensity` weighting and
`narrator_opinion`. Explicit mild or strong input needs a compatible known output. A retained modifier
can carry that degree: `very` plus an unmarked predicate is strong, while `slightly`/`a bit` is mild.
A compatible modifier stays attached through substitution and accent/swear processing. Alternatively,
a certified adjective predicate may express a reviewed modifier's degree itself: `slightly hungry` can become
`peckish`, and `very hungry` can become `starvin'`. Selection, replacement spans and editor alternatives
share this decision, so the modifier is retained or absorbed exactly once. Strong predicates support
reviewed intensifiers including `absolutely` and `really`; `very` plus a lexically mild adjective and
unknown or conflicting compositions still stay as written. Negation is retained. Absorption does not newly enable wider clause expansions, which might discard
frequency or aspect words outside the owned modifier span.

Threshold\-bearing predicates \(`so`, `too`, or a following `enough`) preserve the source's certified
lexical grade even when it's unmarked. An unmarked `hungry enough to…` can't become mild
`peckish enough to…`. Compatible grade is necessary, not proof of exact threshold equivalence across
arbitrary predicates; unsupported or opaque contexts remain conservative. Ordinary inputs with no
stated degree retain unknown\-degree options. Plans'n automatic change alternatives use the same
eligibility. Dictionary discovery remains broader than in\-place grammatical substitution.

Calibration covers DRUNK and HUNGRY. Evidence'n limits are recorded in the
[alcohol degree ledger](../../research/semantic-refinement-2026-10-19/drunk-degree-calibration.md),
[hunger degree ledger](../../research/semantic-followup-2026-10-20/hunger-degree-calibration.md) and
[composition spike](../../research/semantic-spikes-2026-10-20/README.md).

## Noun reference and direct address

A concept's `noun_use` is `any` (default), `reference` or `address`. This distinguishes a quantified reference
such as “Everyone came” from speaking to a group in “Hi everyone”. EVERYONE takes reference; PLURAL_ADDRESS
takes address and offers plural forms such as `you mob` and `youse`. It keeps the existing noun-phrase frame.
A direct `replaces` phrase cannot bypass the concept restriction. An unknown grammatical role satisfies
neither restricted use, leaving the source wording available unchanged.

`takes_addressee: true` declares an expression that introduces a recipient, such as a greeting or thanks.
It is a boolean meaning capability, not a document setting. The reader combines that data with punctuation,
known recipient/name shapes and command grammar. An arbitrary interjection or comma does not prove address.
Simple direct addresses can transform. Ambiguous parentheticals, qualified recipients and unresolved
coordinated recipients stay as written rather than become distributive phrases. A following reference
clause with corroborated finite/governor evidence retains its separate reading. Mere absence of an address
match is not evidence of reference, and a POS guess alone cannot turn a bare command into a finite predicate.
Other noun concepts default to unrestricted use, so “Hello friend”
can still offer `mate`; YOU_PLURAL also remains usable as a subject or object.

## Context and source-English data

`genres.yaml` defines every genre policy and all three embellishment settings. Boolean switches must be
YAML booleans; guidance is text, garnish is a list of known placements or `all`, `keep_share` is a finite
number in 0–1 and `max_length` is finite and at least 1. Custom data directories provide their own policies.
The loader collects malformed genre/dialect data with the other dictionary diagnostics.

`dialect.yaml` maps `us`, `uk` and shared expressions to Australian wording. Values are text or a mapping
with `to`, optional `plural`, `frame`, `known_only` and `not_in`. Replacement/plural values are text and
`known_only` is boolean. `lint_only` flags expressions without automatic replacements. Concept
`not_in` and lexical subject-fit/POS rules keep terms of art and noun/verb senses in their own contexts.
See [translation controls](translation-controls.md) and the executable
[dialect](../../tests/functional/test_dialect.py), [noun phrase](../../tests/functional/test_noun_phrase.py)
and [schema](../../tests/functional/test_schema.py) specifications.

A concept may declare `unless_after: [for, to]` to exclude complements that do not establish its meaning.
The same restriction applies to concept triggers, an entry's direct `replaces` triggers and similarity
fallback. It reads across soft punctuation (commas and dashes), stopping at sentence, semicolon and colon
boundaries. For example, the food-appetite concept leaves “hungry for success” plain; the conservative
restriction also leaves “hungry for lunch” plain until a more specific supported construction is supplied.
The words are dictionary data, not a hunger-specific test in the engine.
Restricted meanings also stay plain when following context is unknown at an incomplete Markdown unit
edge or behind protected code. Opaque content is never read as prose to guess a complement.

## Frame vocabulary

`grammar.yaml` contains `person_nouns` (lower-case noun forms) and `adjective_nouns` (adjective to allowed
following nouns). The same adjective rule applies to attributive matches after a linking verb, so “great
disappointments” cannot evade it through a predicate frame. Multiword person triggers do not make their bare
head a person: “a party animal” does not make an animal a person. Bare person triggers and explicit role nouns
supply the person's vocabulary. Keep genuinely human singular and plural roles in the list.

Plural\-only clothin' forms remain available where they fit. Where a singular agreeing verb must remain, the
engine selects a compatible singular alternative rather than introducing “is my togs”.

Similarity fallback covers slot\-free predicate patterns with a fixed literal shape. Optional\-word patterns
remain supported by exact trigger matching; they aren't guessed through similarity.

Captured noun arguments need a nominal or supported gerund shape: “try hard cheese” and “try running
carefully” have objects, while “try hard to finish” doesn't capture “hard” as an object. A selected form
must retain captured noun/object arguments, either through its slots or identical literal wording. A
slotless variant therefore can't silently drop the tool from “try the tool”.
Short degree/nominal ambiguities such as “a bit harder” or “a little water” stay plain; the tagger alone
can't reliably settle them. Clear nominal constructions such as “a bit of cheese” remain supported.
For an unanchored terminal object slot, temporal signals distinguish “try every day” from “try every
tool”. Preposition\-headed phrases such as “at home” aren't objects. Time words used in anchored arguments,
subjects or nominal compounds remain valid: “give every day a try” and “try every day pass”. Mixed object
and time captures stay plain without trimmin' their spans. This is bounded grammar readin', not a full parse.

Local subject binding follows supported auxiliary chains'n adverbs, including progressive, perfect and
question constructions. It stops at another lexical verb or a clause boundary. This makes optional images
available for “I am feeling hungry” with the correct possessive, without changin' its auxiliary or guessing
a speaker for “feeling hungry”. Writer\-only rewrites still require a writer to preserve tense'n modality.

## Drawl comparison

Phonetic rules can declare `unless_question: true` when their grammatical placement is unsafe in a question.
The guard uses the shared sentence tokenizer, including abbreviations such as `Mr.` and `U.S.`. It applies
only to the declared rule: other grammatical question infixes remain available. Skipped matches keep their
occurrence ordinal so later seeded choices do not shift. The loader requires a real boolean.
Quoted speech can group a declaration and questions in one canonical unit; that whole unit conservatively
skips the opted-in infix. Standalone statements and imperatives remain eligible.

A literal drawl rule may declare `reads_as`, its canonical wording for lint's refrain comparison:

```yaml
- id: want-to-wanna
  match: "(?i)\\bwant to\\b"
  replace: wanna
  reads_as: want to
  prob: 0.6
  min_level: 5
```

Lint reads these annotations from the loaded dictionary, including custom data. This is a comparison spelling,
not a grammatical inverse: ambiguous `yer` is consistently read as `your`. Group-reference replacements and
spelling rules cannot declare `reads_as`. Dropped-g words are also normalised during comparison.

`grammar.yaml` may declare `name_aliases`, a mapping of exact original phrases to accepted comparison wordings.
These only affect lint fidelity, never translation. Keep them narrowly reviewed: a capitalised common phrase
such as `Christmas Trees` can have `Chrissy trees` as an alias without exempting `Christmas Island` or words
inside a person's name. Changed names without an explicit alias retain their warnings.

## Contextual images

`imagery.yaml` is optional for custom data directories. It contains a list of records with unique kebab\-case
`id`, `text`, nonempty `concepts` and `usage`. Concepts must exist in `concepts.yaml`. These include original
comparisons harvested from creative writin', not only attested traditional sayings. Entries remain the home
for reusable slang meanings, such as the `DISHONEST` sense of “as crooked as a dog's hind leg”.

| Field | Values and default |
|---|---|
| `form` | `suffix` (default, a grammatical appendage) or `rewrite` (writer must weave it in) |
| `frames` | Nonempty list of engine frames; defaults to predicate, clause and verb phrase |
| `subject` | `any` (default) or `person`, checked using the existing subject grammar |
| `unless_after` | Optional lowercase complement words; read across soft punctuation within the same clause |
| `related` | Optional reviewed related concept IDs; conditional writer suggestions only |
| `exaggeration` | 0–2, default 1; an eligibility ceiling, not a probability |
| `level` | Minimum level 1–5, default 3 |
| `tone` | `comic` (default), `grim` or `plain` |
| `origin` | `original` (default) or `familiar`; editorial provenance, not proof of attestation |
| `usage` | Required conditions and semantic boundaries for the writer |

Only `{poss}`, `{objposs}` and `{np}` slots are supported. Plans bind them only when the detection supplies
the required subject, object or noun phrase; bare lookup returns an explicitly unbound `template` card.
Unknown fields, concepts, frames, slots, invalid ranges'n duplicate IDs fail loading. Vulgarity is derived
from `swears.yaml` and can't be supplied to bypass the cap. Negative source contexts suppress meaning\-based
imagery. The matching is deterministic'n conservative, rather than full logical or discourse analysis.
See [selection and configuration](translation-controls.md#contextual-imagery) for the distinction between
writer suggestions'n automatic insertion. Historical round replays remove images referencing temporarily
set\-aside concepts in scratch only, while still rejecting genuinely unknown concepts.

## Finite clauses and sense boundaries

Question realisation supports modular subject/be/have/do clauses'n existential there/be clauses. How good is that?
have inverts directly; lexical possession takes do\-support. Fixed finite or negative clause idioms remain
available in declarations but are declined in questions when no safe modular question form exists. An outer
auxiliary such as “could” can't be left before a replacement that brings its own independent finite clause;
predicate alternatives remain available, preservin' the original auxiliary.

Ambiguous bare “establish” remains unchanged; unambiguous founding phrases retain their idioms. Restless
“turning and tossing” is held apart from throwing an object. Truthful assurance (“in all honesty”) can use
“hand on heart”, while wholehearted devotion and bare sincere/solemn manner stay distinct. These are sense
and grammar rules shared by all document presets; their tests are
[the fidelity regressions](../../tests/functional/test_fidelity_maintenance.py).

## Reviewed sense boundaries

A shared concept expresses the meaning actually established by its triggers. Physical solitude doesn't
establish emotional loneliness; a shout doesn't establish a reprimand; very little isn't exactly zero.
Named tree species, animals, baggage, package contents'n construction methods need explicit support in
the input. Compatible grammatical entries preserve source modals, object/reference slots'n location nouns
rather than silently droppin' them. These distinctions live in dictionary data'n reuse the existin'
meaning'n frame checks; optional writer imagery doesn't redefine a literal mapping.

Historical `sandy blight` remains available for casual eye-inflammation wording. Its concept declares
`not_in: [technical, official, instructions]`, honoured when those domains appear in resolved
`document_config.term_domains`. A document classifier supplies presets; no separate hidden type-specific
rule is added. Exact terms and precise protected wording keep their ordinary document-policy behaviour.

Automatic beer\-package mappings require an explicit twenty\-four\-unit amber fluid package: a 24\-pack, twenty\-four
pack, or case/carton of 24 coldies. A bare case/carton may carry a different count, including in a later
qualifier, so it stays plain. The slab expression remains in the dictionary'n discoverable by lookup;
this factual boundary doesn't introduce a quantity parser.

Terminal object'n noun captures must reach a complete argument. A coordinated listener, partial multiword
name, possessive noun head or of\-qualified name stays plain when the capture can't retain it. A following
coordinated verb or fresh finite clause remains independent. The same bounded check protects speech,
scolding'n other verb constructions; it doesn't claim a full parser for arbitrary coordination.

Waltzing Matilda requires an explicitly travellin' swag carrier. Humpin' the bluey alone can use the separate
baggage expression; walking country roads alone doesn't establish baggage. Exact\-zero mappings also
exclude minimising nothing\-much constructions, which may describe a small amount rather than none.

### Figurative predicate objects

Source triggers can capture the object of a figurative predicate through `{np}`. `sick of work` and
`tired of life` resolve to FED_UP; literal SICK/TIRED readings are restricted through `unless_after`.
Their object must survive automatic substitution. If a current target cannot bind it, translation and
plans keep the source; lookup can still explain a relevant standalone idiom. `tired from work` and
`sick with flu` retain their literal readings. See the [source spike](../../research/semantic-spikes-2026-10-20/README.md).


Negative VP forms beginnin' with do\-support \(`don't` plus a base verb\) realise according to the
source verb: finite forms inflect do, an outer modal/infinitive retains its own auxiliary, and
perfect/progressive forms retain their participle. This keeps grammatical negation in the phrase
without special rules for a particular dictionary word. The source reader records the local VP
auxiliary, including inverted questions.


A `number: count` form that supplies its own indefinite article requires a determined or explicitly
counted source phrase. It cannot create a serving from unmeasured mass wording. Counts such as one,
another and several keep their determiner and suppress the target's extra article across modifiers.
The same number check is used for selected replacements and their alternatives. A noun used as a
modifier can be excluded with the existing `grammar.nominal_roles: [head]` requirement.


## Evidence calibration and v4 data

The evidence weights are versioned in `attestation.yaml`. Version `20261114-source-hunt-1` follows the
source\-hunt reconciliation'n a 300\-term curator sanity check. It keeps the existin' assessor and
testimony ceiling; an edited scholarly dictionary reaches four bars, while crowd\-only evidence stays
below that threshold. The [calibration ledger](../../research/gate4-evidence-2026-11-14/README.md)
records source scopes, dates, before/after scores'n remainin' limits. An attestation score isn't an
Australian\-commonness estimate or a certificate for every mapping.

The data model now accepts optional `other_sense`, a non-empty single-line curator note describing an
entry's other everyday meaning. It supports the source-owned-term reader; the note alone
does not establish a sense. Concepts may carry curated directed `near` relations, each with `concept`,
reader-facing `differs`, and `setting` (`dinkum` or `troppo`). Unknown, self and duplicate targets fail
validation. The v4 working runtime uses only these curated relations for automatic stand-ins at genuinely wordless
spots. Dinkum takes a 0.5 probability multiplier and Troppo 0.75; Deadset takes none. Existing level,
region, register, theme, frame and vulgarity gates still apply. News, instructions, technical, official
and custom document types disable automatic near use. Exact entries, even if blocked by the current
dials, prevent it. Lookup may explain relations at Deadset without enabling automatic replacement;
the coordinated [v4 contract](../contracts/v4/README.md) is frozen.


An adverb entry may declare `grammar: {position: before_verb}`. Source grammar must establish the
actual lexical verb; the renderer moves the adverb before that verb and retains its bound text.
Without that evidence the candidate is unavailable. The default `source` position is unchanged.


## Aiming at the dials

`dial_mode` is one request choice for rudeness and embellishment together: `aim` or `cap` (default).
`--dial-mode aim` is the CLI spelling; MCP uses the same `dial_mode` parameter and default.
Aim favours permitted words near the requested vulgarity and gives Dinkum/Troppo their own garnish rates,
limits and spacing. Clean choices remain possible; semantic, grammatical, theme and document restrictions
are unchanged. Explicit document/profile overrides win, including zero. The level dial is unchanged.
Cap retains the historical permission-only profiles and seeded translation choices. Aim deliberately
changes seeded choices, so a host should persist its mode beside the other dials for replay/share calls.
The frozen v4 response and pin schemas are unchanged. Dictionary identity changes with the aim data.

The tunin' is in `data/dial-goals.yaml`; original profile data remains in `data/profiles.yaml`.


## Phrase emphasis and model-only contrasts

The final phonetic pass gives an emphasis edit ownership of its matched phrase'n following head for
prefix insertions. Ownership follows every length\-changin' pass. A later infix or emphatic tail can't
claim the same head. Engine\-generated degree\-modifier swaps'n adjective stacks already allocate emphasis;
ordinary drawl/spellin' still apply. Independent phrases remain independent. Source degree wording such
as flamin' can take one generated infix; caller\-owned literal wording remains exact. Changes\-card alternatives
recompute their own allocation through the same rule. This applies in both aim'n cap, and can correct
seeded outputs that previously contained competing emphasis devices.

`lookup-contrasts.yaml` holds reviewed, mutually exclusive lexical poles within a named distinction.
Each pole has `words` (lower\-case English phrases'n explicit inflections\) and `concepts` (known IDs,
possibly empty when that pole has no dedicated meaning\). If the query positively asserts one pole,
model\-only inference can't use concepts from another pole. Negated words don't assert that pole;
a query namin' several poles is ambiguous'n supplies no such veto. Explicit term discovery and
established non\-model evidence keep their priority. These words are neither source triggers nor new
search aliases, and add no meanings or entries. Both scalar'n batched lookup use this gate.

The initial distinctions cover soft/loud/no speech, small/large physical size, and low/high price.
This is a bounded, authored safeguard, not a claim that cosine similarity proves synonymy or that all
possible antonyms have been enumerated. Negation/anchor checks remain separate'n the model threshold
is unchanged. Invalid concepts, duplicate words or conflicting pole memberships fail dictionary loading.
